results.question: Is spending on track?
results.tagged:
Recorded spending is below plan in both broad views of the sample: costed activities are Rs 51.96 crore below plan across 20 Gram Panchayats, while approved activities are Rs 41.61 crore below plan across 20 Gram Panchayats. [d1-36141] [d1-44064]

Biswamathpur warrants early reconciliation because it has the largest recorded gap in both views: Rs 7.23 crore, or 13.9%, for costed activities and Rs 6.74 crore, or 16.2%, for approved activities. [d1-36141] [d1-44064] It accounts for only 4.3% of costed activities and 4.0% of approved activities, and its recorded approved-activity ratio is 0.0%. [d1-36141] [d1-44064] Kalimela is next, with gaps of Rs 5.90 crore for costed activities and Rs 5.46 crore for approved activities. [d1-36141] [d1-44064]

The thematic view also shows gaps spread across several areas. [d1-46782] [d1-46331] [d1-45814] Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village—is Rs 20.13 crore below plan across 16 blocks; Sheragada has the largest share at 16.7% or Rs 3.36 crore, followed by Rangeilunda at 15.4% or Rs 3.11 crore. [d1-46782] Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village—is Rs 13.11 crore below plan across 16 blocks; Kalimela leads at 25.5% or Rs 3.34 crore, followed by Rangeilunda at 14.1% or Rs 1.85 crore. [d1-45814] Theme 5—Clean and Green Village—is Rs 8.62 crore below plan across 9 districts; Ganjam accounts for 36.8% or Rs 3.17 crore, followed by Bargarh at 21.1% or Rs 1.82 crore. [d1-46331]

Review should therefore combine reconciliation of Biswamathpur and Kalimela’s approved and costed records with thematic follow-up in Sheragada, Rangeilunda and Ganjam; the remaining gaps are distributed across many other Gram Panchayats, blocks and districts rather than being confined to these locations. [d1-36141] [d1-44064] [d1-46782] [d1-45814] [d1-46331]

results.question: How is Chikilli doing?
results.tagged:
Chikilli has a sizeable planned portfolio, but recorded spending remains well below plan and its sanction pipeline is the lowest in the 20-Gram-Panchayat sample. Planned cost totals Rs 5.51 crore across 640 activities, while spending is Rs 4.12 crore below plan. [d1-29225] [d1-29231] Across all fiscal years, Chikilli has the lowest sanctioned amount and proposed cost at sanction among the sampled Gram Panchayats; it also has the lowest number of activities with technical and administrative approval in 5/6 fiscal years, with no clear pattern in 2023-2024. [1-01299] [1-01309] [1-01301] [1-01305]

The portfolio is heavily oriented towards Theme 6 - Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village, which accounts for 59.5% of planned cost (Rs 3.27 crore) and 48.4% of the 640 activities. [d1-29225] The same theme accounts for 63.4% of the shortfall against plan (Rs 2.61 crore below plan), with spending at 20.2% as a ratio. [d1-29231] Planned money on abandoned works totals Rs 46.72 lakh, led by Theme 6 at 43.7% (Rs 20.44 lakh) and Theme 5 - Clean and Green Village at 33.8% (Rs 15.77 lakh). [d1-29228]

Recorded spending totals Rs 1.39 crore across 6 fiscal years, without a single year dominating; 2021-2022 accounts for 22.9% (Rs 31.82 lakh) and 2024-2025 for 19.2% (Rs 26.63 lakh). [d3-01701] Spending linked to planned activities totals Rs 1.30 crore, and the linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across these six years; this movement should be treated as improved recording completeness unless the cashbook total also increased. [d2-01636]

Most activities remain recorded as approved: 550 of 640 activities, or 85.9%, are under “Activity Approved.” [d1-29298] At the same time, 93.1% of the Rs 1.63 crore general-component spending—Rs 1.52 crore—is associated with “WORK ONGOING,” although that status covers 10.2% of the 640 activities. [d1-29303] Record classification also warrants attention, as 412 activities, or 64.4% of the portfolio, are uncategorised by asset category. [d1-29312]

results.question: Where is money planned but not spent?
results.tagged:
At Gram Panchayat level, the recorded shortfall between planned and measured spending is Rs 7.23 crore in Biswamathpur [d1-28967], Rs 5.60 crore in Bheden [d1-28703], Rs 4.75 crore in Boipariguda [d1-29024], Rs 2.90 crore in Dutimendi [d1-29842], Rs 1.94 crore in Bandhpali [d1-27925] and Rs 1.88 crore in Mendarajpur [d1-32203]. Further gaps are Rs 1.27 crore in Hirlipali [d1-30622], Rs 1.02 crore in Andhrua [d1-27660], Rs 90.62 lakh in Haldikudar [d1-30370] and Rs 69.45 lakh in Barimunda [d1-28178].

The gap is spread across many asset categories in most of these Gram Panchayats, rather than being confined to one category. [d1-27925] [d1-28178] [d1-29842] [d1-32203] [d1-28703] [d1-28967] [d1-30370] Uncategorised activities nevertheless account for substantial shares in several places, including 37.3% or Rs 2.09 crore in Bheden [d1-28703], 31.5% or Rs 91.35 lakh in Dutimendi [d1-29842], and 23.6% or Rs 1.70 crore in Biswamathpur [d1-28967]. The gap is more concentrated in Hirlipali, where Uncategorised accounts for 59.0% or Rs 75.10 lakh [d1-30622], and Andhrua, where it accounts for 50.1% or Rs 51.17 lakh [d1-27660].

Some specific sectors also merit attention: in Boipariguda, Rural housing accounts for 44.9% or Rs 2.13 crore and Drinking water for 26.5% or Rs 1.26 crore of the gap [d1-29024]; in Mendarajpur, Buildings accounts for Rs 31.04 lakh and Irrigation Sources for Rs 30.00 lakh [d1-32203]; and in Haldikudar, Water Sources & Structures accounts for 24.1% or Rs 21.81 lakh [d1-30370].

Across the 10 Gram Panchayats whose office internet and computer status is recorded as “Not ready”, spending measured against plan is Rs 27.80 crore below plan. [d1-13071] Kalimela accounts for Rs 5.90 crore and Bheden for Rs 5.60 crore, while the remaining 8 Gram Panchayats account for Rs 16.30 crore. [d1-13071]

At district level, Bargarh and Ganjam have the lowest spending measured against plan across 6/7 LSDG theme values. [1-03549] The exception is Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village—where Ganjam and Malkangiri are the lowest. [1-03549]

results.question: How is Barpali block doing?
results.tagged:
Barpali accounts for 48.4% [d4-02188] of Bargarh district’s recorded spending, at Rs 2.64 crore [d4-02188], and 47.3% [d4-02188] of the district’s 3,062 activities [d4-02188]. Within Barpali, the 1,447 planned activities [d3-00232] are almost evenly divided between Bandhpali, with 729 [d3-00232], and Bhatigaon, with 718 [d3-00232]. Spending is also broadly balanced: Bandhpali records Rs 1.40 crore [d4-00583] and Bhatigaon Rs 1.24 crore [d4-00583]. The block has 21 plans [d4-00577], comprising 12 in Bandhpali [d4-00577] and 9 in Bhatigaon [d4-00577].

Recorded planned cost is Rs 5.49 crore [d4-00581], compared with spending of Rs 2.64 crore [d4-00583], leaving spending Rs 2.85 crore below plan [d3-00238]. Bandhpali accounts for 68.2% [d3-00238] of this gap, or Rs 1.94 crore below plan [d3-00238], and has a spending-to-plan ratio of 41.9% [d3-00238]; Bhatigaon is Rs 90.49 lakh below plan [d3-00238]. Cost and sanction records also need attention: 1,067 planned activities have no recorded cost [d4-00580], while the Rs 2.96 crore sanctioned amount [d1-09520] covers only activities with a sanction record on file—about one in six [d1-09520].

There are 171 ongoing activities [d3-00244], split closely between Bhatigaon with 88 [d3-00244] and Bandhpali with 83 [d3-00244]. All 6 activities under approval [d1-09528] are in Bandhpali, while Bhatigaon has 0 [d1-09528].

Spending linked to planned activities totals Rs 2.55 crore [d2-00151], divided between Bandhpali at Rs 1.34 crore [d2-00151] and Bhatigaon at Rs 1.20 crore [d2-00151]. The linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across six years [d2-00151]; this should be read as improved recording completeness unless the cashbook total rose alongside it, rather than as evidence of higher spending [d2-00151]. In the general-component thematic view, spending totals Rs 2.99 crore across 7 LSDG theme values [d1-09543], led by Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village—at 33.1% or Rs 99.22 lakh [d1-09543], and Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village—at 30.6% or Rs 91.57 lakh [d1-09543].

The next review should prioritise reconciliation of the plan-to-spending gap, particularly in Bandhpali [d3-00238], completion of missing activity costs and sanction records [d4-00580] [d1-09520], and verification that improved plan–payment linkage is consistent with the cashbook [d2-00151].

results.question: Tell me about untied grants.
results.tagged:
Records classified as Untied contain Rs 16.95 crore of planned works across 19 Gram Panchayats, with no single GP dominating: Sharagada has the largest share at 8.5% (Rs 1.44 crore), followed by Kalimela at 7.1% (Rs 1.21 crore), while the other 17 account for Rs 14.30 crore. [d1-48891] Within the XV Finance Commission scheme, untied-grant plans total Rs 8.91 crore across 19 Gram Panchayats; Sharagada again has the largest share at 11.4% (Rs 1.02 crore), followed by Kalimela at 6.8% (Rs 60.54 lakh), with Rs 7.29 crore across the remaining 17. [d1-42176]

Code 101 accounts for the majority of untied-grant planning in 19/20 Gram Panchayats, with Boipariguda as the exception. [1-01631] Within Code 101, planned untied grants total Rs 35.37 crore, but the sanctioning authority is not recorded for 2,309 rows representing 70.4% of the total (Rs 24.89 crore); the 12 recorded authority values together account for Rs 10.48 crore. [d1-36910] Among sanctioning-authority values, Sarpanch accounts for the majority in 5/6 fiscal years, with 2022-2023 showing a different pattern. [1-00801]

Planning is predominantly associated with Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village—in 18/20 Gram Panchayats. [1-01793] The exceptions are Boipariguda, where Unmapped LSDG theme has the highest planned amount, and Kalimela, where Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village—is highest. [1-01793] Boipariguda also stands out within rural housing, accounting for 95.7% (Rs 2.13 crore) of the Rs 2.23 crore planned across 20 Gram Panchayats, although it holds 2.0% of the 305 activities; the other 19 Gram Panchayats together account for Rs 9.50 lakh. [d1-24172]

Across every fiscal year, the Mixed social-composition group has the highest planned untied-grant amount. [1-01256] Across all social-composition groups, ALL/General public accounts for the majority of planned untied grants by intended beneficiary. [1-02478]

results.question: Anything I should be looking at in Ganjam?
results.tagged:
In the 20-Gram-Panchayat sample, Ganjam merits review for gaps between plans, sanctions and recorded spending. Spending is Rs 17.85 crore below plan across 3 blocks: Rangeilunda accounts for 51.0% (Rs 9.11 crore below plan), Sheragada for 25.9% (Rs 4.63 crore below plan), and Khallikote for Rs 4.12 crore below plan; Rangeilunda’s ratio is 23.1%. [d3-01190] Ganjam is also among the lowest-spending districts against plan in 6/7 LSDG themes alongside Bargarh; for Theme 4 - Water Sufficient Village, Ganjam and Malkangiri are the lowest. [1-03549]

Sanction records should be reconciled with plans and spending. The recorded sanctioned amount is Rs 6.30 crore, of which Rangeilunda has 56.5% (Rs 3.56 crore), Sheragada 43.5% (Rs 2.74 crore), and Khallikote Rs 0. [d3-01188] At Gram-Panchayat level, Sharagada accounts for 43.5% (Rs 2.74 crore) and Biswamathpur for 29.2% (Rs 1.84 crore), while the other 2 Gram Panchayats account for Rs 1.72 crore; however, the sanction basis covers only activities with a sanction record on file, about one in six. [d1-14749] Across the wider sample, spending measured against sanction is evenly spread across focus areas in 19/20 Gram Panchayats; Chikilli is the only exception and may warrant a focus-area-level check. [1-01723]

Planning-record quality also needs attention. There are 1,768 activities planned without a cost across 4 Gram Panchayats, including 722 in Sharagada and 421 in Mendarajpur. [d4-02684] Planned money on abandoned works totals Rs 1.91 crore, with Sharagada accounting for 62.1% (Rs 1.19 crore), compared with its 33.8% share of the 2,723 activities. [d1-14747] Sharagada should therefore be specifically reviewed for costless plans, abandoned works and sanction documentation. [d4-02684] [d1-14747] [d1-14749]

Finally, Rs 5.65 crore of spending is linked to planned activities across 4 Gram Panchayats, led by Sharagada at 31.4% (Rs 1.78 crore) and Biswamathpur at 23.8% (Rs 1.35 crore). [d2-00761] The linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across six years, but this indicates greater recording completeness unless the cashbook total rose alongside it; the plan-to-payment linkage should therefore be reconciled with cashbooks before interpreting the increase as higher spending. [d2-00761]

results.question: What is the position on abandoned works?

[d1-44212] Sharagada has the largest share at 20.3% (Rs 1.19 crore), followed by Bheden at 15.0% (Rs 87.81 lakh), while the other 16 Gram Panchayats together account for Rs 3.78 crore. [d1-44212] Bargarh records the highest planned amount among districts. [1-03578]

A separate reconciliation issue requires attention: records under “WORK ONGOING” also contain Rs 25.45 lakh in planned money identified with abandoned works across all 20 Gram Panchayats. [d1-44561] This amount is concentrated in Kalyansinghpur at 42.5% (Rs 10.81 lakh) and Bandhpali at 37.9% (Rs 9.64 lakh); the remaining 18 Gram Panchayats account for Rs 5.00 lakh. [d1-44561] These records should be checked to confirm whether the activity status and abandoned-work classification are aligned. [d1-44561]

Sanitation has the highest number of abandoned activities in 7/9 districts, with no clear pattern in Koraput or Kandhamal. [1-01277] In planned-money terms, Maintenance and New/Fresh works lead across population-size bands, while Theme 5 – Clean and Green Village and Theme 6 – Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village lead across social-composition groups. causal_log_lines.question: Which blocks account for the shortfall?

sentences.sentence: It holds 9.2% of the 12,704 activities but 17.5% of the spending shortfall, making it the clearest block for initial review, while reconciliation should still cover all 16 blocks because most of the shortfall is distributed among the others.
Biswamathpur warrants early reconciliation because it has the largest recorded gap in both views: Rs 7.23 crore, or 13.9%, for costed activities and Rs 6.74 crore, or 16.2%, for approved activities.

Review should therefore combine reconciliation of Biswamathpur and Kalimela’s approved and costed records with thematic follow-up in Sheragada, Rangeilunda and Ganjam; the remaining gaps are distributed across many other Gram Panchayats, blocks and districts rather than being confined to these locations.
